title: Lecture 12 Boss Problems
subtitle: Problem solving with loops: the while loop

clearance.starter:
DISCOUNT_RATE = 0.25
price = float(input('First price: $'))
rows = int(input('Rows: '))
count = 0

print('Original Discount Sale')

# Write the loop here.
clearance.check:
import re
assert re.search(r"^\s*while\b", __code__, re.M), "Repeat the work with a while loop."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*for\b", __code__, re.M), "Use a while loop; for is not part of this lecture."
assert __code__.count("DISCOUNT_RATE") >= 2, "Work out the discount with price * DISCOUNT_RATE instead of writing 0.25 again."
assert re.search(r":[^}]*\.2f\}", __source__), "Show every amount with :.2f in the f-string."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 2, "Print one row per pass with a single print() inside the loop, and keep the heading print() outside it."
assert count == rows, "Add 1 to count on every pass so the loop stops after rows passes."
hints: Loop while `count < rows`. On each pass, `discount` is `price * DISCOUNT_RATE` and the sale price is `price - discount`.
Print the three amounts in one f-string with `:.2f` after each and one space between them. Then add 5 to `price` and 1 to `count`.
clearance.answerNote: Both price and count are updated on every pass. When rows is 0, the first test is false, so only the heading is printed.

teams.starter:
first = int(input('First group: '))
second = int(input('Second group: '))
team_size = min(first, second)

# Decrease team_size until it divides both groups.

print('Largest shared team size:', team_size)

cases.name: Typed 120 and 48
cases.expected: First group: Second group: Largest shared team size: 24

cases.name: Typed 7 and 5
cases.expected: First group: Second group: Largest shared team size: 1

cases.name: Typed 36 and 36
cases.expected: First group: Second group: Largest shared team size: 36

cases.name: Typed 9 and 27
cases.expected: First group: Second group: Largest shared team size: 9

cases.name: Typed 1 and 40
cases.expected: First group: Second group: Largest shared team size: 1

teams.check:
import re
assert re.search(r"^\s*while\b", __code__, re.M), "Repeat the work with a while loop."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*for\b", __code__, re.M), "Use a while loop; for is not part of this lecture."
assert "%" in __code__, "Use % to test whether team_size divides a group exactly."
assert "gcd" not in __code__ and "import" not in __code__, "Search for the answer with the loop; do not import a module."
assert re.search(r"team_size\s*-=\s*1\b|team_size\s*=\s*team_size\s*-\s*1\b", __code__), "Decrease team_size by 1 on each pass."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Keep the single print() after the loop."
hints: The starter sets `team_size` to the largest size that could work. Try smaller sizes one at a time by subtracting 1 from `team_size` on each pass.
A size divides a group exactly when `first % team_size` is 0. Keep looping while at least one of the two remainders is not 0.
For 120 and 48 the search starts at 48 and stops at 24, the first size where both remainders are 0. A size of 1 divides every group, so the loop always stops.
teams.answerNote: The loop continues while at least one group has a remainder. A team size of 1 divides every positive group size, so the search always stops.

binary.starter:
bits = input('Binary: ')
index = 0
value = 0

# Process one character on each pass.

print('Decimal:', value)
binary.check:
import re
assert re.search(r"^\s*while\b", __code__, re.M), "Repeat the work with a while loop."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*for\b", __code__, re.M), "Use a while loop; for is not part of this lecture."

assert "len(bits)" in __code__, "Test index against len(bits) so every character is processed once."
assert "bits[index]" in __code__, "Pick one character out of bits with bits[index]."
assert not re.search(r"int\(\s*bits\s*,", __code__), "Build the value one digit at a time; int(bits, 2) is not part of this course."
assert re.search(r"\*\s*2\b|\b2\s*\*", __code__), "Double the value built so far before adding the new digit."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Keep the single print() after the loop."
hints: The starter sets `index` and `value` to 0. Loop while `index < len(bits)`, look at one character with `bits[index]` on each pass, and add 1 to `index` at the end of the pass.
`int(bits[index])` turns the character `'1'` into the number 1 and `'0'` into 0.

Reading left to right, every digit already in `value` is worth twice as much once one more digit arrives. Replace `value` with `value * 2 + int(bits[index])`. For `101101` the value goes 1, 2, 5, 11, 22, 45.
binary.answerNote: Multiplying by 2 makes room for the next binary digit. The index starts at 0 and advances once per pass, so every character is processed exactly once.

circle.starter:
terms = int(input('Terms: '))
step = 1
denominator = 1
sign = 1
estimate = 0.0

# Add one term and print one estimate on each pass.
circle.check:
import re
assert re.search(r"^\s*while\b", __code__, re.M), "Repeat the work with a while loop."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*for\b", __code__, re.M), "Use a while loop; for is not part of this lecture."
assert "math" not in __code__ and "import" not in __code__, "Build the estimate with the loop; do not import a module."
assert re.search(r":[^}]*\.6f\}", __source__), "Show the estimate with :.6f in the f-string."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Print one estimate per pass with a single print() inside the loop."
assert denominator == 2 * terms + 1, "Add 2 to denominator on every pass so it moves through 1, 3, 5, 7 and so on."
assert sign == (1 if terms % 2 == 0 else -1), "Flip sign on every pass so the terms alternate between adding and subtracting."
assert step == terms + 1, "Add 1 to step on every pass and stop after terms passes."
hints: Loop while `step <= terms`. On each pass add one term to `estimate`, print, then update `denominator`, `sign` and `step`.
The term is `sign * 4 / denominator`. `sign` is 1 when adding and -1 when subtracting, so `sign = -sign` flips it for the next pass.
After the print, add 2 to `denominator` (1, 3, 5, 7 and so on), flip `sign`, and add 1 to `step`. The first pass adds 4/1 and prints 4.000000; the second subtracts 4/3 and prints 2.666667.
circle.answerNote: The denominator advances through the positive odd integers, while sign = -sign alternates addition and subtraction. The inclusive test produces exactly the requested number of lines.
